title: Thousands Around Us: Numbers up to 9,999

standard_text: Numbers up to 9,999: thousands, hundreds, tens and ones, reading, writing and comparing 4-digit numbers (summary of NCERT Maths Mela Class 4)
meta_desc: Class 4 Thousands Around Us worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 4): thousands, place value, expanded form, number names, comparing. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 10 hundreds = 1 thousand. 4,536 has 4 thousands, 5 hundreds, 3 tens and 6 ones.
  • Read it as four thousand five hundred and thirty-six.
  • Compare the thousands, then the hundreds, and so on.

Examples

Example

What is 1,000 more than 3,507?

Add 1 to the thousands

Answer: 4,507

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing four thousand and seven as 4007 with the wrong zerosFill empty places with 0: 4,007.
Comparing by the last digitStart with the biggest place.

faq.q: How many hundreds make a thousand?

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 8 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 8 hundreds = 800. The digit is 8, but its value is 800.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 8 is in the tens place, so it is worth 8 tens = 80. The digit is 8, but its value is 80.

items.q: In 9,247, which digit is in the hundreds place?
items.e: 9,247 has 9 thousands, 2 hundreds, 4 tens, 7 ones. The hundreds digit is 2.

items.q: In 7,209, which digit is in the tens place?
items.e: 7,209 has 7 thousands, 2 hundreds, 0 tens, 9 ones. The tens digit is 0.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 2 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 2 hundreds = 200. The digit is 2, but its value is 200.

items.q: In 5,496, which digit is in the thousands place?
items.e: 5,496 has 5 thousands, 4 hundreds, 9 tens, 6 ones. The thousands digit is 5.

items.q: In 4,973, which digit is in the hundreds place?
items.e: 4,973 has 4 thousands, 9 hundreds, 7 tens, 3 ones. The hundreds digit is 9.

items.q: In 1,359, what does the digit 3 stand for?
items.e: Read the places from the left: thousands, hundreds, tens, ones. The 3 is in the hundreds place, so it stands for 3 hundreds, or 300.

items.q: In 7,956, what does the digit 5 stand for?

items.q: In 8,201, what does the digit 2 stand for?

items.q: What number is 4,000 + 700 + 8?
items.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 in any empty place: 4,000 + 700 + 8 = 4,708.

items.q: 3,000 + ☐ + 70 + 4 = 3,574. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 3,574 has 5 in the hundreds place. 5 hundreds = 500, so the missing part is 500.

items.q: 8,000 + 400 + ☐ + 7 = 8,437. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 8,437 has 3 in the tens place. 3 tens = 30, so the missing part is 30.

items.q: What number is 2,000 + 200 + 9?
items.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 in any empty place: 2,000 + 200 + 9 = 2,209.

items.q: Estimate the number the arrow points to.
items.e: Each small mark is 1,000. The arrow is between 2,000 and 3,000, closer to 3,000. So it shows about 2,800.

items.q: What is 1,000 less than 7,068?

items.e: 1,236 has 1 thousand. Take it away and the thousands digit becomes 0: 1,236 − 1,000 = 236.

items.q: What is 1,000 more than 8,905?

items.q: What is 1,000 less than 3,004?

items.e: Each number is 6 more than the one before. 36 + 6 = 42.

items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 5 tens is more than 2 tens. So 4,352 > 4,325.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 8 hundreds is more than 6 hundreds. So 1,862 > 1,682. 1,862 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 9 tens is more than 8 tens. So 6,798 > 6,789. 6,789 is the smallest.

items.q: Put 6,472, 6,427, 6,742 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 6,427 < 6,472 (tens: 2 < 7). 6,472 < 6,742 (hundreds: 4 < 7). So the order is 6,427, 6,472, 6,742.

items.q: Put 8,627, 8,276, 8,726 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 8,276 < 8,627 (hundreds: 2 < 6). 8,627 < 8,726 (hundreds: 6 < 7). So the order is 8,276, 8,627, 8,726.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: The arrow is to the left of 0, so the number is negative. Count back from 0: −1, −2, −3. The answer is −3.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: The arrow is to the left of 0, so the number is negative. It is 2 marks past −5: count −6, −7. The answer is −7.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: The arrow is to the left of 0, so the number is negative. Count back from 0: −1, −2, −3, −4. The answer is −4.

items.q: What temperature does the thermometer show?
items.e: The red line ends below 0, so the temperature is negative. Each mark is 1 degree. Count down from 0: −1, −2, −3, −4, −5, −6. It shows −6 °C.

items.q: What temperature does the thermometer show?
items.e: The red line ends below 0, so the temperature is negative. Each mark is 1 degree. Count down from 0: −1, −2. It shows −2 °C.

A shop has 4 boxes of 1,000 stickers, 12 packs of 100 stickers and 6 single stickers. How many stickers is that?
items.e: 12 hundreds = 1 thousand and 2 hundreds. So there are 5 thousands, 2 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones: 4,000 + 1,200 + 6 = 5,206.

items.q: Use each of the digits 3, 8, 0 and 5 once to make the greatest 4-digit number.
items.e: Put the biggest digit in the thousands place, then the next biggest, and so on: 8, 5, 3, 0. The greatest number is 8,530.

items.q: Eggs come in boxes of 6. How many eggs are in 9 boxes?
At 7:00 am the temperature was −3 °C. By lunchtime it was 4 degrees warmer. What was the temperature at lunchtime?
items.e: Warmer means count up. From −3 °C count up 4: −2, −1, 0, 1. Do not skip 0. It was 1 °C.

items.q: Meera's dad is a lorry driver. He has driven 3,950 km this month. Next month he will drive 1,000 km more than this. How far will he drive next month?
items.e: 1,000 more: only the thousands digit changes. 3 thousands → 4 thousands. 3,950 + 1,000 = 4,950 km.

items.q: Kabir's family parks in a car park. The ground floor is level 0. The floors below ground are level −1, level −2 and so on. He gets into the lift on level 2 and goes down 4 levels. Which level is he on now?
items.e: Count down 4 from level 2: 1, 0, −1, −2. Do not skip level 0. He is on level −2.

items.q: Each bench in the school hall seats 9 children. How many children can sit on 7 benches?
items.e: Count in 9s seven times: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63. 7 × 9 = 63 children.

items.q: Gauri counts on in 1,000s from 2,450: 2,450, 3,450, … What is the 5th number she says?
items.e: Write the 5 numbers: 2,450, 3,450, 4,450, 5,450, 6,450. The 5th number is 6,450.

items.q: Last year 5,083 people visited a castle. This year 1,000 fewer people visited. How many people visited this year?
items.e: 1,000 fewer: only the thousands digit changes. 5 thousands → 4 thousands. 5,083 − 1,000 = 4,083.

items.q: In the evening the temperature was 3 °C. During the night it fell by 5 degrees. What was the temperature then?
items.e: Fell means count down. From 3 count down 5: 2, 1, 0, −1, −2. Do not skip 0. It was −2 °C.
